rows: Ground squirrels have two kinds of colour-sensing cells in their eyes, where people have three.

A ground squirrel can see a light flicker on and off up to 108 times a second. To a person, a light that flickers faster than about 60 times a second looks steady. Fast movements look slower to a squirrel, so this view runs slowly and then jumps ahead to catch up.
A squirrel’s eyes sit on the sides of its head, which probably gives it a wide view with less detail than yours. This part of the view is a guess.
